items.title: Felda settler dies in suspected axe attack
items.summary: A local source said the suspect was reportedly running amok by the roadside near his house while wielding a weapon believed to be an axe. The source said nearby residents were afraid to intervene because the suspect was armed. "Villagers did not dare to intervene because the suspect was holding an axe and running amok," the source said.

items.title: UN probe accuses Israel of 'extermination' in West Bank
items.summary: GENEVA: Israel has committed the crime against humanity of "extermination" in the West Bank, while continuing to commit "genocide" against Palestinians in the Gaza Strip, United Nations-mandated investigators said Monday. The UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry said Israeli forces had also committed other crimes against humanity and war crimes in the West Bank, which Israel has occupied since 1967. The commission, which does not speak for the UN itself, first determined in a September 2025 report that Israel had committed "genocide" in the war in Gaza following Hamas' deadly October 7, 2023 attack on Israel - a finding Israel flatly rejects.

items.title: Lufthansa returns to KL, plans daily Frankfurt flights in 2027
items.summary: Lufthansa Group senior vice president global sales Frank Naeve said the service reconnects two important cities and regions, creating opportunities for business and trade between Malaysia, Germany and Europe. Naeve said Lufthansa will increase the frequency to daily flights starting next year's summer schedule. He said the direct connection carries economic significance for Malaysia.

items.title: M'sia committed to providing RM100mil in reconstruction aid to Gaza - Mohamad
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia remains committed to providing RM100 million in reconstruction aid to Gaza, as announced by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim last year, but its implementation has been hampered by the deteriorating security situation in the territory. Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said the aid would be implemented when conditions on the ground were more conducive, to ensure its effective delivery. Meanwhile, Mohamad said that he would seek clarification from Myanmar over claims that about 300 of its citizens, who were repatriated from Malaysia, were still being detained by the military in Yangon.

items.title: Longtime SJ Securities CEO Azman Manaf passes at 65
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Datuk Ahmad Azman Abdul Manaf, managing director and CEO of SJ Securities Sdn Bhd for 30 years, has passed away over the weekend. Azman joined SJ Securities as managing director in 1996. SJ Securities is a licensed broker regulated by the Securities Commission and Bursa Malaysia.

items.title: Indonesian NGO alleges 21 Malaysian-linked firms involved in forest fires
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Indonesian environmental non-governmental organisation Wahana Lingkungan Hidup Indonesia (WALHI) has claimed that 21 companies linked to business groups with Malaysian ties were involved in forest and land fires in Indonesia between January and September 2026. The findings are part of a mapping analysis report titled "Who Are Behind the Fires?" WALHI said forest and land fires in Indonesia should not be viewed merely as technical errors or negligence by local companies holding permits.

items.title: Pahang Astro Awani journalist dies at 66
items.summary: KUANTAN: Astro Awani senior journalist Mohd Zailani Md Atan, who was based in Pahang, died at his home here today. Zailani, 66, died in his sleep about 5pm. Zailani leaves behind a wife and four children.

items.title: Two motorcyclists killed after car skids into opposite lane
items.summary: Iskandar Puteri district police chief Assistant Commissioner Radin Ramlan Radin Taha said the accident occurred when the car driver lost control of the vehicle while negotiating a wet bend. He said the car then veered into the opposite lane before crashing into the two motorcycles. Radin said the car driver and two passengers suffered minor injuries.

items.title: Haze eases as Kuala Lumpur skyline returns to clear view
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Genting Highlands, the Petronas Twin Towers and the city skyline are back in clear view as haze eases across the Klang Valley. The sky is indeed clear in KL this morning," wrote X user @1Obefiend, sharing photos of blue skies and distant hills. the user wrote.

items.title: West River secures RM17.85m residential M&E subcontracts
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: ACE Market-listed integrated mechanical and electrical (M&E) engineering services provider West River Bhd has secured two residential engineering subcontracts with a combined value of RM17.85 million. The contracts comprise an RM11.0 million electrical works subcontract for a residential project in Puchong, Selangor, and an RM6.85 million air conditioning and mechanical ventilation (ACMV) nominated subcontract for Park Green at Pavilion Bukit Jalil, Kuala Lumpur. Both contracts were secured via its wholly-owned subsidiary, West River Engineering Sdn Bhd (WRE).

items.title: News@9: Today's top headlines - October 26, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: Blunt-force trauma A 73-year-old doctor killed in yesterday's landslide died from blunt-force trauma and breathing difficulties, a post-mortem found. Samsuri seeks fairness PN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar says the coalition could perform better in GE16 with a level playing field. Akmal secures payment Umno Youth chief Datuk Dr Akmal Saleh has secured funds to pay Teresa Kok RM300,000 in a defamation case.

items.title: Nepal turns to SMART’s drones, detection gear after declining two Malaysian rescue offers
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 26 — Malaysia’s third offer to assist Nepal in its search and rescue (SAR) operations for mud flood victims was accepted after two earlier offers were turned down, paving the way for the deployment of the Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (SMART), equipped with technical expertise and advanced detection equipment. SMART commander Senior Fire Superintendent 1 Abdul Manaf Che Isa, who led the mission, said Malaysia initially offered to send 50 rescuers, followed by a second offer of 25 personnel with SAR equipment, but Nepal declined both offers because it already had sufficient rescue teams. He said Nepal’s government eventually accepted Malaysia’s third offer, which involved deploying just 11 SMART personnel, nine high-capacity drones and specialised detection equipment, after several rounds of discussions.

items.title: KKB's unit wins RM49.8mil arbitration against Shapadu Energy Services
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: OceanMight Sdn Bhd, a subsidiary of KKB Engineering Bhd, has successfully secured a nearly RM49.8 million arbitration award against Shapadu Energy Services Sdn Bhd (SES), concluding a corporate dispute that first came to light in late 2023. The tribunal ruled in OceanMight's favor, ordering SES to pay a total combined sum of RM49.78 million. The tribunal's decision, dated Oct 12, also carries a mandatory interest penalty.

items.title: Sarawak live pig imports to Selangor under strict controls since July 2025
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The import of live pigs from Sarawak to Selangor since July 2025 has been carried out with approved import licences and is subject to strict control procedures. He said Sarawak Minister of Food Industry, Commodity and Regional Development Datuk Seri Dr Stephen Rundi Utom had announced the matter in July 2025 during an official loading ceremony at Pending Port, Sarawak. Chan said Selangor Infrastructure and Agriculture Committee chairman Datuk Izham Hashim had also explained that the state government allowed the issuance of import licences for live pigs from Sarawak, subject to strict conditions and control procedures.

items.title: Malaysia seeks Myanmar's explanation over 300 repatriated detainees
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia will seek an explanation from Myanmar over reports that about 300 nationals repatriated from Malaysia remain detained at a military facility in Yangon. Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said Malaysia's chargé d'affaires in Myanmar would investigate the reports and provide an update. "If there are reports that 300 people are still being detained, we will ask the Myanmar government to inform us.

items.title: Ministry revokes 28,401 business licences over illegal activities by foreigners
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Housing and Local Government Ministry revoked 28,401 business licences nationwide over the past three years as part of efforts to curb illegal business activities by foreigners. Its minister Nga Kor Ming said the ministry conducted 10,248 integrated enforcement operations nationwide to address the issue and protect the interests of local business owners. Nga said the ministry took the matter seriously and had implemented strict enforcement measures to ensure compliance with business licensing requirements.

items.title: Court of Appeal reduces Klang council's damages from RM117mil to RM3mil
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Court of Appeal today reduced the damages payable by the Klang Municipal Council, now known as the Klang Royal City Council, to property developer NBC Land Sdn Bhd from RM117 million to RM3 million in a dispute over the rehabilitation of a former dumpsite. "The parties agreed to share this estimated cost of RM6 million equally, 50 percent each (RM3 million each)," he said. Therefore, he said the court substitute the High Court's award with RM3 million in damages, representing the council's agreed 50 per cent share of the RM6 million rehabilitation cost.

items.title: RMAF gears up for first FA-50M fighters this Friday
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) is prepared for the arrival of its FA-50M light combat aircraft, with the necessary infrastructure, personnel and maintenance support in place. Earlier, Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said Malaysia would receive its first two FA-50M light combat aircraft on Friday as part of efforts to strengthen its air combat capabilities. "The aircraft would complement, rather than replace, the RMAF's existing Sukhoi Su-30MKM and F/A-18D Hornet fighter aircraft.

items.title: UNHCR has failed to resettle refugees in third countries, says Mohamad
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) has failed to resettle refugees in third countries, says Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan. He said most Rohingya refugees in Malaysia held UNHCR cards, but the agency had resettled only about 5,000 refugees over the past two to three years. "The majority of these Rohingya refugees are UNHCR cardholders.

items.title: Malaysia's invitation to Palestinian leader Abbas remains open
items.summary: SLUG: OPENDOOR Malaysia's invitation to Palestinian leader Abbas remains open Amalia Azmi, Nor Ain Mohamed Radhi news@nst.com.my KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's invitation to Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas to visit the country remains open, although a date has yet to be fixed. Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said he had extended the invitation verbally on several occasions, and Abbas had expressed deep appreciation for Malaysia's support for the Palestinian struggle for a sovereign state. ENDS KEYWORDS: Malaysia, Malaysia News, NST, nation, Dewan Rakyat, Mahmoud Abbas, Palestine, Mohamad Hasan, Tok Mat, Wisma Putra, invitation © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Abang Johari confirms AI data centre plan in Sarawak under US$50b investment
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 26 — The US$50 billion investment announced by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim recently includes strategic plans by a major international company to develop an artificial intelligence (AI) data centre in Tanjung Embang. Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg said further details, including the name of the company involved, could not be disclosed at this stage to preserve the confidentiality of the corporate transaction. The Premier said the international technology giant had chosen Kuching as its investment destination because it viewed Sarawak as a forward-looking state that was aggressively transitioning towards a new economy.

items.title: Boy seriously injured after being hit at pedestrian crossing near school
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: An 11-year-old boy was seriously injured after being hit by a car while crossing the road outside Sekolah Kebangsaan Darau in Manggatal. He said the boy was crossing the road from right to left at the pedestrian crossing when the car approached. Closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage of the incident went viral on social media earlier, showing the boy being hit while crossing the road.

items.title: Edelteq acquires 51pct stake in factory automation company Nixma
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Edelteq Holdings Bhd is acquiring a 51 per cent stake in factory automation solutions provider Nixma Technology (M) Sdn Bhd for RM15.3 million. In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, the company said it entered into agreements with Nixma's vendors on Oct 26 to acquire 15 per cent of the company's enlarged share capital for RM4.5 million and subscribe for new shares representing another 36 per cent for RM10.8 million. Nixma designs and assembles factory automation products, including leak detection, assembly and testing, robotic, and high-precision automation solutions.

items.title: Britons top list of drug mule suspects arrested at KLIA, RM202.76mil in drugs seized
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 77 cases linked to drug mule syndicates at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) were recorded between January and Oct 15, resulting in the arrest of 93 people. Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the cases involved the seizure of 2,526.28kg of drugs worth an estimated RM202.76 million. He said the seized substances comprised 2,407.27kg of cannabis (64 cases), 77.837kg of methamphetamine (four cases), 22.11kg of ketamine (four cases), 15.585kg of cocaine (three cases), and 3.475kg of a ketamine and cannabis mixture (two cases).

items.title: Live pig imports from Sarawak to Selangor subject to strict controls since July 2025, says deputy minister
items.summary: He said Sarawak Minister of Food Industry, Commodity and Regional Development Datuk Seri Dr Stephen Rundi Utom had announced the matter in July 2025 during an official loading ceremony at Pending Port, Sarawak. Further clarification had also been provided by Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup, who was then Deputy Agriculture and Food Security Minister, and by Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu through oral question sessions and written replies in the Dewan Rakyat. Chan said Selangor Infrastructure and Agriculture Committee chairman Datuk Izham Hashim had also explained that the state government allowed the issuance of import licences for live pigs from Sarawak, subject to strict conditions and control procedures.

items.title: Melaka polls: PH strategy pragmatic, but CM candidate needed
items.summary: Universiti Utara Malaysia political analyst Professor Dr Azizudin Md Sani said PH appeared to be prioritising winning as many constituencies as possible, with the question of who would lead the state government taking a back seat. Azizudin said that while PH could delay naming its chief ministerial candidate, announcing one could strengthen its chances by giving voters a clearer leadership alternative. In the 2021 state election, Barisan Nasional won 21 of Melaka's 28 seats, while PH secured five and Perikatan Nasional two, giving BN a commanding majority in the state assembly.

items.title: Thailand's Phuket hit by flash flooding and landslides [WATCH]
items.summary: BANGKOK: Heavy rain has triggered flash floods and landslides on the Thai island of Phuket, with the weather authority forecasting more bad weather ahead of the end of the rainy season in the southeast Asian country, reported German Press Agency (dpa). Floodwaters carried rocks, mud and debris into residential areas and shopping streets, damaging houses, shops and vehicles, the Bangkok Post reported on Monday, citing authorities. After persistent rain, water and debris flowed down the hillsides into lower-lying areas overnight.

items.title: Asia Brands' non executive director Lim Weng Khuan passes
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Asia Brands' Bhd announced the demise of Datuk Dr Lim Weng Khuan. Lim was appointed as an independent, non-executive director of Asia Brands on Aug 29, 2022. He had over 34 years of experience in industrial relations and human resource management in Lion Group, F&N Group, HSBC Bank and Tan Chong Group.

items.title: Radzi hints at Umno return through Rumah Bangsa initiative
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: After nearly a decade away from Umno, Tan Sri Mohd Radzi Sheikh Ahmad has hinted at rejoining the party through its Rumah Bangsa initiative. The development was shared by Radzi, a former Umno secretary-general, during a visit to the party's current secretary-general, Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki, today. He also held several cabinet positions, including deputy minister in the Prime Minister's Department, deputy home minister and home minister.

items.title: Malaysia to push for Asean haze framework at Manila meeting
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia will table a non-paper on transboundary haze at the Asean Foreign Ministers' Meeting in Manila, the Philippines, on Nov 14. Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said the proposal seeks to establish a framework for Asean member states to support one another whenever forest fires or haze hit the region. "I plan to propose discussions on establishing a proper framework to address transboundary haze, so that Asean member states can support one another whenever forest fires or haze affect the region," he said while winding up the debate on his ministry's 2027 Budget in the Dewan Rakyat today.

items.title: Unitrade secures manufacturing rights for Finnish waste management tech in Johor
items.summary: The group announced that its indirect 60-per cent-owned subsidiary, Winnson Ecotech Sdn Bhd, entered into a technology transfer and licensed manufacturing agreement with Molok on Oct 26. Molok, headquartered in Ylöjärvi, Finland, is a waste collection solutions specialist and part of the European pre-collection waste management leader, SULO Group. Under the agreement, Molok will transfer its manufacturing technology and know-how to Winnson Ecotech to locally produce the Molok Classic semi-underground waste collection container.

items.title: Indonesian firefighters give thanks as rain arrives after four months [WATCH]
items.summary: KALIMANTAN: After months of battling forest and land fires, fire-fighting volunteers in South Kalimantan, Indonesia, were moved to tears when rain finally fell, bringing relief to the fire-hit area. Data for Oct 1 to 14 showed that forest and land fires had affected 1,754.30ha in South Kalimantan. Heavy rain also drenched Banjarbaru on the afternoon of Oct 25, helping to extinguish fires and improve air quality.

items.title: Court of Appeal slashes Klang council’s RM117m dumpsite damages bill to RM3m
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 26 — The Court of Appeal today reduced the damages payable by the Klang Municipal Council, now known as the Klang Royal City Council, to property developer NBC Land Sdn Bhd from RM117 million to RM3 million in a dispute over the rehabilitation of a former dumpsite. “The parties agreed to share this estimated cost of RM6 million equally, 50 percent each (RM3 million each),” he said. Therefore, he said the court substitute the High Court’s award with RM3 million in damages, representing the council’s agreed 50 per cent share of the RM6 million rehabilitation cost.

items.title: Zahid extends aid to two Bernama, NST journalists injured in Ipoh-Lumut road crash
items.summary: IPOH, Oct 26 — Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has extended financial assistance and words of encouragement to two journalists from the Malaysian National News Agency (Bernama) and the New Straits Times (NST) who were injured in a road accident on the Ipoh-Lumut road yesterday. Speaking at Zahratulhayat’s residence in Klebang Harmoni, Shuhaimi said Ahmad Zahid had also pledged to monitor their recovery and provide further assistance where needed. Shuhaimi said Ahmad Zahid appreciated the solidarity and moral support shown by the Ipoh media fraternity towards the injured journalists.

items.title: Dewan Rakyat Speaker asks Rayer to write formally over Takiyuddin’s ‘munafik’ remark
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 26 — Jelutong Member of Parliament RSN Rayer has been asked to write an official letter to Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul if he wants Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan (PN-Kota Bharu) to be referred to the Parliament Rights and Privileges Committee. Johari said that the committee will examine the matter regarding Takiyuddin’s use of the word “hypocrite” (munafik), which was linked to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim during the debate on the 2027 Budget last Monday, before making any decision. Johari explained that he had previously asked Takiyuddin to retract the word, but the PAS Secretary-General, via a letter dated October 22, suggested that a mediation process be held without retracting the word.

items.title: Melaka schools to remain open amid haze, outdoor activities suspended if API exceeds 100
items.summary: MELAKA, Oct 26 — All educational institutions under the Ministry of Education (MOE) in Melaka will operate as usual tomorrow, said the Melaka State Education Department. In a statement, the Melaka Education Department announced that outdoor classroom activities may proceed as usual in areas recording an Air Pollutant Index (API) reading below 100. However, the department stated that all outdoor activities, including physical education, co-curricular and sports activities, camps, celebrations, assemblies, and activities in open halls, must be suspended if the API reading exceeds 100, in line with MOE Circular No.

items.title: Fuziah: PKR fields seven new faces among nine candidates for Melaka polls
items.summary: MELAKA, Oct 26 — Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) is fielding seven new faces among its nine candidates in the upcoming Melaka state election, reflecting its push for leadership renewal. Its secretary-general Datuk Dr Fuziah Salleh said the new faces make up 77.8 per cent of the party’s line-up, including four young candidates. She said three women are also among the candidates, accounting for 33.3 per cent of the party’s total.

items.title: British nationals top KLIA drug mule arrests, drugs worth RM202.76m seized
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 26 — A total of 77 cases linked to drug mule syndicates at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) were recorded between January and Oct 15, with 93 individuals arrested. Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said these cases involved the seizure of 2,526.28 kilogrammes (kg) of drugs, with an estimated value of RM202.76 million. He said the seized substances comprised 2,407.27 kg of cannabis (64 cases), 77.837 kg of methamphetamine (four cases), 22.11 kg of ketamine (four cases), 15.585 kg of cocaine (three cases), and 3.475 kg of a mixture of ketamine and cannabis (two cases).

items.title: MACC seeks 24-year-old man to assist Sabah corruption probe, last traced to Semporna
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 26 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) is seeking a local man to assist in an investigation in Sabah. In a statement today, MACC identified the man as Jamaluddin Jamahali, 24, who is being investigated under Section 17(b) of the MACC Act 2009. Anyone who knows his whereabouts or has relevant information is urged to contact investigating officer Abu Hudzaifah Abd Talib at 014-8573727 or via email at hudzaifah@sprm.gov.my.

items.title: Zahid rejects RM2.1b overspending claims, says ministry underspent revised allocation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 26 — Rural and Regional Development Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi today dismissed claims that his ministry overspent by RM2.1 billion, saying the figure reflected the difference between its original allocation and revised spending ceiling over three years. Winding up the 2027 Budget debate in the Dewan Rakyat, Zahid said the ministry spent RM6.108 billion between 2023 and 2025, against a revised allocation of RM6.143 billion after additional funding was approved, Free Malaysia Today reported. According to Johan, spending on rural road projects reached RM1.8 billion in 2023 against an approved allocation of RM1.1 billion, RM2 billion in 2024 compared with RM1.3 billion allocated, and RM2.3 billion in 2025 against RM1.6 billion approved.

items.title: Langkawi’s duty-free overhaul: RM300,000 vehicle price cap and RM10,000 spending limit
items.summary: Deputy Finance Minister Liew Chin Tong said changes to the duty and tax exemption policy for vehicles were introduced not only to address revenue leakage but also to discourage such business practices. Liew acknowledged that some business operators would be affected by the policy but stressed that local residents would not be impacted. Earlier, he said that, effective Jan 1, 2026, duty and tax exemptions for vehicles would be capped at a value of RM300,000 to prevent wealthy individuals from abusing the incentives to acquire luxury vehicles.

items.title: Pakatan ties, Perikatan disciplinary action on agenda at Bersatu meeting tonight
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Oct 26 — Bersatu’s supreme leadership council is set to meet tonight to finalise, among other matters, the party’s political cooperation plans ahead of the 16th Melaka state election. As reported by Harian Metro , the meeting, chaired by Bersatu president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin, is understood to begin at 8pm at the party’s headquarters in Petaling Jaya. Bersatu has recently been linked to a possible electoral cooperation pact with Pakatan Harapan (PH) for the Melaka polls.

items.title: Flight attendant charged over drunk driving crash that killed DBKL road crew on Lebuhraya Sultan Iskandar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 26 — A flight attendant pleaded not guilty at the Magistrate’s Court here today to two charges of driving under the influence of alcohol, causing the death of a supervisor and injuring a lorry driver in an accident on Lebuhraya Sultan Iskandar here on Saturday (Oct 24). Mohd Iman Nafiz Fong Mohd Sabirin, 26, is accused of driving with a blood alcohol concentration of 64 milligrams (mg) per 100 millilitres (ml) of blood, exceeding the legal limit of 50mg per 100ml, and causing the death of Faris Irfan Fazli, 29, on Lebuhraya Sultan Iskandar heading towards Jalan Parlimen at 4.09 am on Oct 24. If convicted, the accused may also be disqualified from holding or obtaining a driving licence for a period of at least 10 years from the date of conviction.

items.title: Sepang eyes F1 return with Cabinet proposal due in November
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 26 — The Sepang International Circuit (SIC) is drafting a feasibility study on bringing back the Formula One (F1) Grand Prix (GP) to Malaysia, to be presented to the Cabinet in November. SIC chief executive officer Azhan Shafriman Hanif said it was currently holding engagement sessions with the government, relevant agencies and industry players to obtain accurate information and data for inclusion in the study. He said the findings would serve as one of the factors for the government to consider before deciding whether Malaysia should return as host of the prestigious race.

items.title: Loke defends DAP’s seat reduction for Melaka poll as tactical shift for better odds
items.summary: MELAKA, Oct 26 — DAP’s decision to contest only seven seats in the 16th Melaka state election, including its decision not to field a candidate in Bemban, was based on an assessment of its chances of winning, party secretary-general Anthony Loke said. He said the decision took into account DAP’s performance in the 2021 state election, when the party finished second in several seats it failed to win, but came third in Bemban. That is why we are contesting only seven seats this time.

items.title: Malaysia targets bankruptcy discharges in under 36 days next year
items.summary: Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said the initiative under the Fast Track Discharge Programme would be implemented through the Malaysian Insolvency Department (MdI). Azalina said the government had also strengthened its recovery efforts through the Second Chance Policy, which recorded 253,457 bankruptcy discharges from 2023 to September 2026. Azalina said the digitalisation of MdI services also enabled bankruptcy discharge applications to be submitted online through the e-Insolvensi portal.

items.title: High Court dismisses ex-student’s RM400,000 suit over phone seizure during SPM trial exam
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Oct 26 — The Kuala Terengganu High Court has upheld the dismissal of a RM400,000 negligence and defamation suit filed by a former student against her teachers and the government over a body search and the seizure of her mobile phone during an SPM trial examination six years ago. The court ruled that while the school was entitled to confiscate Nabilah’s mobile phone, it had no authority under Education Ministry guidelines or school examination regulations to inspect its contents. Checks on the phone uncovered notes, examination questions and answer schemes for several subjects.

items.title: Major legal win for Ampang Jaya residents as court allows challenge to council’s development plan
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 26 — The High Court’s decision to grant leave to 12 Ampang Jaya residents to initiate judicial review proceedings challenging the Ampang Jaya Municipal Council Local Plan 2035 (RT MPAJ 2035) marked a significant step forward for local community rights. In a statement, residents’ action group TOLAK RT2035 claimed that the local plan, gazetted on Feb 6, 2025, contained fundamental flaws and unpublicised land-use conversions. They further claimed that the local plan did not incorporate the objections raised during the 2022 public objection hearing.

items.title: Pensioner charged in Kangar with sexual assault, using criminal force against two preteen girls
items.summary: KANGAR, Oct 26 — A government retiree pleaded not guilty in the Sessions Court here today to three charges of committing physical sexual assault and criminal force against two girls about two months ago. The first two charges alleged that Annuar committed physical sexual assault for sexual purposes against an 11-year-and-five-month-old girl at a house at No. The first two charges were brought under Section 14(a) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017, which provides for a maximum prison sentence of 20 years and whipping upon conviction.

items.title: Dr Mahathir absent from SG4 forum due to health issues, Mokhzani reads keynote
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 26 — Former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad was unable to attend the SG4 Business and Economic Forum 2026 at the Kuala Lumpur Convention Centre today due to health reasons. His son, Tan Sri Mokhzani Mahathir, said the 101-year-old statesman had prepared his keynote speech and intended to deliver it himself, but had been feeling unwell in recent weeks, Berita Harian (BH) reported. Datuk Seri Mukhriz Mahathir was also present.

items.title: Dr Akmal Saleh willing to sit out Melaka polls if court case hurts BN chances
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Oct 26 — Umno Youth chief Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh says he is prepared to give up his bid to defend the Merlimau state seat in the Melaka election on November 14 if the court case he faces hurts Umno and Barisan Nasional’s chances at the polls. According to Berita Harian , Dr Akmal said he had conveyed his position to Barisan Nasional chairman and Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, stressing that the party’s interests must come before his personal ambitions. The 38-year-old said Umno had entrusted him with defending the Merlimau seat, although the final decision would only be known on nomination day.

items.title: AKPS rolls out hologram technology to help travellers navigate arrival procedures
items.summary: SEPANG, Oct 26 — The Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) has developed hologram technology to be deployed at the satellite building of Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) Terminal 1, to assist travellers in obtaining information regarding arrival procedures in the country. He noted that the development of this hologram was inspired by an initiative from the Ministry of Home Affairs (KDN), which installed a hologram of the Minister of Home Affairs, Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail, in the lobby of the Setia Perkasa Complex. “Just as the Ministry of Home Affairs placed a hologram of the Minister in the lobby of the Setia Perkasa Complex, AKPS shares the same vision and mission.

items.title: Orang Asli in remote Kelantan and Terengganu areas urged to evacuate early as monsoon looms
items.summary: GUA MUSANG, Oct 26 — Orang Asli living in remote areas have been urged to move to safe locations immediately if faced with the threat of floods, sudden torrents or landslides during the Northeast Monsoon (MTL), without waiting for conditions to become critical. Kelantan and Terengganu Orang Asli Development Department (JAKOA) director Mohd Faedzyal Mohamed said all Tok Batin (Orang Asli village heads), penghulu (sub-district chiefs) and Orang Asli Village Development and Security Committees had been instructed to step up preparedness for the 2026/2027 Northeast Monsoon, which is expected to begin tomorrow and last until March next year. Mohd Faedzyal said village leaders needed to identify high-risk areas, monitor weather changes and river levels, and identify residents who might require immediate assistance during emergencies.

items.title: Former Court of Appeal judge Mahadev Shankar dies at 94, leaves enduring legal legacy
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 26 — Former Court of Appeal Judge Datuk Mahadev Shankar, renowned for his legal acumen, language mastery, and enduring contributions to Malaysian jurisprudence, died at Shah Alam Hospital at 2 am today. His close friend, Malaysia-India Heritage Society founder-president Prabhakaran Nair, said funeral arrangements would be announced later. Mahadev was also recognised for his contributions to legal scholarship.

items.title: Lynas waste disposal facility reaches 77pc completion as 2031 deadline looms
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 26 — The permanent disposal facility (PDF) for radioactive waste generated by Lynas Malaysia Sdn Bhd had achieved 77 per cent completion in construction and operations as of Aug 31, with 1.45 million metric tonnes of the 1.467 million metric tonnes of Water Leach Purification (WLP) waste generated having been transferred to the facility. Chang said Lynas was required to stop generating WLP radioactive waste before March 2031, while existing waste and waste generated during the period must be treated to reduce its activity concentration to below one becquerel (Bq) per gram using methods proven effective through research and development (R&D). After the five years, if Lynas is still generating radioactive WLP waste, the JTA may suspend or revoke the licence.

items.title: Loke says RM1,000 driver aid not a Melaka poll sweetener, rollout continues nationwide
items.summary: MELAKA, Oct 26 — Transport Minister Loke Siew Fook has denied that the RM1,000 special financial assistance given to taxi, rental car and school bus drivers in Melaka today was intended to fish for votes ahead of the Melaka state election. “I am distributing the assistance in Melaka today. Taxi and rental car drivers in every state nationwide will receive this assistance,” he said.

items.title: Dr Akmal Saleh’s lawyers to file second representation after prosecutors reject bid to drop charge
items.summary: BUKIT MERTAJAM, Oct 26 — Prosecutors have rejected a representation by Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh seeking to have a charge against him dropped, prompting his lawyers to submit a second appeal to the Attorney General. His lead counsel, Aizat Azam, said the defence has applied to file a second representation to the Attorney General, setting out the facts and legal arguments relating to the case, Sinar Harian ( SH ) reported. Speaking outside the Bukit Mertajam Court Complex today, Aizat said the first representation, filed in December 2025, was rejected and the decision conveyed during today’s case mention.

items.title: ‘No compromise’: Selangor exco backs police probe into drug stash at Klang temple
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 26 — The Selangor state government will not tolerate the use of any place of worship for criminal purposes, regardless of the religion, race or background of those involved. Selangor Human Resources and Poverty Eradication Committee chairman V. Papparaidu said he took seriously media reports about drugs being found at an unregistered place of worship in Klang during an operation by the Selangor Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department from Oct 13 to 19. “Places of worship should be respected, kept sacred and provide peace to their respective congregations, not be used to store prohibited substances or facilitate criminal activities,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: MoHE urges off-campus students to report residential addresses for monitoring
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 26 — The Higher Education Ministry (MoHE) has stressed that students living in rented accommodation off campus should inform their universities of their place of residence to facilitate monitoring. Its minister, Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir, said monitoring was difficult because some students arranged their own rental accommodation without going through their universities. Zambry said some public universities and polytechnics worked with their student affairs divisions to manage accommodation in designated areas, while some students opted to rent accommodation independently.
